one_line: Poet-king of the Qutb Shahi dynasty who founded Hyderabad and nurtured Dakhni literature.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s to early 30s, medium height, lean but regal build with a graceful posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with a warm wheat-brown complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed medium-length black beard and moustache, sharp dark eyes with long lashes, arched brows, and a default expression of calm intelligence with a slight poetic half-smile.
appearance.hair: Black hair kept short and tidy under a tall conical Deccani turban in rich emerald green silk with fine gold stripes and a subtle wrapped tail at the back, adorned with a single small red stone brooch at the front.
appearance.costume: He wears a long, fitted Deccani jama (robe) reaching mid-calf, in deep maroon silk with narrow vertical gold zari stripes and a wrapped overlap closing slightly to the right, belted at the waist with a broad cream-gold woven sash; underneath are slim ivory-coloured churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, and on his feet soft brown leather mojari shoes with slightly upturned toes; over his shoulders rests a lightweight pale turquoise muslin shawl with a simple gold border, draped neatly but leaving his arms mostly free; he has modest jewellery: a single strand of small pearls close to the neck, a simple gold ring on his right hand, and small gold stud earrings, all consistent with a late 16th-century Deccan sultan’s courtly attire.
appearance.signature: A rolled manuscript tied with a red cord in his left hand, representing his Kulliyat and Dakhni poetry, and a sheathed, slightly curved Deccani talwar with a simple steel hilt and plain brown leather scabbard hanging at his left hip as a symbol of rulership rather than active battle.

ref_desc: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is a wheat-brown, oval-faced young Deccani sultan with a neat black beard, emerald conical turban, maroon striped silk jama, ivory churidar, turquoise shawl, pearl necklace, carrying a red-tied manuscript and a sheathed talwar at his hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah as a dignified late 16th-century Deccan sultan: a wheat-brown, oval-faced young man with sharp dark eyes, neat medium-length black beard and moustache, and a calm, thoughtful expression with a slight poetic half-smile. He wears a tall conical Deccani turban in rich emerald green silk with fine gold stripes and a small red stone brooch at the front, his black hair short and hidden beneath it. His main garment is a long, fitted maroon silk jama reaching mid-calf, patterned with narrow vertical gold zari stripes, wrapped and overlapping slightly to the right, belted with a broad cream-gold woven sash tied firmly at the waist. Underneath, show slim ivory churidar trousers gathered at the ankles and soft brown leather mojari shoes with gently upturned toes. Over his shoulders, drape a pale turquoise muslin shawl with a simple gold border, light and flowing yet modest, leaving his arms mostly free. Add modest jewellery: a single strand of small pearls around his neck, a plain gold ring on his right hand, and tiny gold stud earrings. At his left hip hangs a slightly curved Deccani talwar in a plain brown leather scabbard with a simple steel hilt, worn as a symbol of sovereignty rather than an aggressive weapon. In his left hand he holds a rolled manuscript tied with a red cord, signifying his Dakhni Kulliyat. Keep the palette dominated by deep maroon, emerald green, ivory, pale turquoise, and gold, and present him from multiple angles to clearly show face, turban, robe, sash, shawl, trousers, shoes, manuscript, and sword for consistent redrawing.
